title: Component Layout and Theming knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Component Layout and Theming”?
options: Component Layout and Theming means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Component Layout and Theming removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Component Layout and Theming should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Component Layout and Theming helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Component Layout and Theming helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Component Layout and Theming is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Layout components” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Layout components” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Layout components” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Layout components” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Layout components” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Layout components” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Layout components” under Component Layout and Theming. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Component Layout and Theming”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
